name: Slack

field_reviews.reason: docs.slack.dev confirms Slack apps install via the v2 OAuth 2.0 authorization flow yielding scoped bot/user tokens; the MCP server likewise uses confidential OAuth with client_id/client_secret.
OAuth v2 flow plus bearer-token authentication for Web API calls both confirmed in live Slack developer docs.

App creation at api.slack.com/apps is self-serve and installable to a free workspace; note some workspaces require admin approval, and MCP specifically is restricted to directory-published or internal apps.
Web API spans messaging, channels, users, files, canvases, search, admin; plus Events API and Socket Mode.
HTTP Web API (rest), Socket Mode WebSocket delivery, and the official MCP server (JSON-RPC 2.0 over Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.slack.com/mcp) all confirmed live.

Official Slack MCP server verified at docs.slack.dev/ai/slack-mcp-server (endpoint mcp.slack.com/mcp, confidential OAuth, tools for search/messaging/canvases/users, requires a registered Slack app; Marketplace-published or internal apps only). Composio SLACK toolkit page confirms 167 tools, 9 triggers, OAuth2, Composio-managed app.
Self-serve app registration and free workspaces; complete public docs.
No blocker for standard API integration; the unlisted-app restriction applies only to the MCP surface, not the Web API.

notes: Re-opened Slack's live MCP server docs (endpoint, JSON-RPC/Streamable HTTP, OAuth endpoints, scope tables), OAuth install docs, and the Composio SLACK toolkit page (167 tools/9 triggers). All eight fields supported as drafted. Minor nuance: Slack MCP is limited to Marketplace-published or internal apps — worth carrying into mcp_notes but not a field error.
